title: Google Brings Agentic Video AI to YouTube, Cutting Analysis Costs by 66%
excerpt: A new Gemini feature lets AI dynamically navigate video timelines instead of processing every frame, with plans to power YouTube's Ask tool in coming months.
body:
• Google has launched "agentic video understanding" for its Gemini AI models, letting the system dynamically navigate video timelines instead of processing every frame.
  • The feature reduces token consumption by up to 88% and analysis costs by up to 66% while improving accuracy by about 7% on long-form content.
  • Available now through the Gemini API for Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash Lite, the feature will soon power YouTube's "Ask YouTube" watch-page tool.
  • Google also plans to bring the conversational "Ask" experience to the wider YouTube search, letting users query video content directly.

Google has introduced a new AI capability called "agentic video understanding" that fundamentally changes how its Gemini models process video content. Instead of ingesting every frame at a fixed rate, the models can now autonomously navigate video timelines, loading only the segments relevant to a query.

The feature, announced September 1 on Google's AI blog, is available immediately through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. It works with video uploads and YouTube videos across three models: Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash Lite.

How It Works

Gemini's default video mode uses static processing, capturing one frame per second and feeding the entire sequence to the model. That approach works for short clips but becomes expensive and imprecise for longer content — a 90-minute lecture at 1 FPS generates thousands of frames, most of them irrelevant to a specific question.

Agentic video understanding replaces this with a dynamic loop. The model decides what to watch, how quickly to examine it, and which modality to use — frames, audio, or transcript. It invokes an internal tool to load only the relevant portion of the video file, effectively turning the AI into an active investigator rather than a passive viewer.

"Instead of static processing where the model ingests media streams at a fixed frame rate, agentic video understanding enables Gemini to take an active, goal-directed role in determining what to watch."

— Google AI Blog

The practical benefits are substantial. Google reports that across standard video analysis benchmarks, the agentic approach reduces token consumption by up to 88%, cuts analysis costs by up to 66%, and improves accuracy by roughly 7% compared to static processing. The gains are most pronounced on long-form content — from 10-minute how-to guides to multi-hour recordings.

Applications Beyond Simple Summarization

The feature supports several specific use cases that static processing struggles with. Sub-second moment retrieval can pinpoint split-second state changes and tight cut boundaries that 1 FPS sampling misses. Long-form needle-in-a-haystack search can answer complex queries across multi-hour videos without consuming millions of tokens. The system can also detect anomalies by resampling interesting time windows at higher frame rates, and count repeated actions or objects over time.

Google says developers can enable the feature by setting the processing parameter to "agentic" in their API configuration, with no additional fee beyond standard Gemini API token pricing.

Coming to YouTube's Ask Feature

The broader consumer impact will come when agentic video understanding powers YouTube's "Ask YouTube" feature on the video watch page. Google confirmed this will happen "in the coming months," using Gemini to provide answers grounded in the actual visuals of videos users are watching.

Google has also signaled plans to bring the conversational "Ask" experience to the wider YouTube search, according to Search Engine Journal. The feature already exists in limited form — users can ask Gemini to summarize videos, answer context-based questions, and explain topics without interrupting playback. Adding agentic processing would make these responses significantly more accurate and cost-efficient at scale.

YouTube's help page for the search version states that its ranking system "prioritizes relevance, engagement, and quality," similar to regular YouTube search, though it offers no additional detail on how videos are selected as citations in AI-generated responses.

What This Means for Content Creators

For the millions of Indian content creators on YouTube — India is the platform's largest market by user count — the shift raises questions about discoverability. Google has not yet provided guidance on how creators should adapt their videos for AI-driven analysis systems. The technology could reshape how educational, cooking, and tutorial content is consumed, allowing viewers to extract specific answers without watching entire videos.

The feature is available now for developers through the Gemini API. Consumer rollout across the Gemini app and YouTube's watch-page Ask feature is expected in the coming months.
